title: 1990 AHSME Problem 10
statement: An \(11\times11\times11\) wooden cube is formed by gluing together \(11^3\) unit cubes. What is the greatest number of unit cubes that can be seen from a single point?

solutions.text:
From a suitable point one can see three mutually adjacent faces. They contain \[ \begin{aligned} &3(11^2)-3(11)+1\\ &=363-33+1\\ &=331 \end{aligned} \] distinct unit cubes: subtract the three shared edges and restore the corner cube.

Thus the correct answer is D.
hints: At most three faces of a cube are visible from one point
Use inclusion-exclusion on three mutually adjacent \(11\times11\) faces
